page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-96-highlssd is a high-capacity storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for data-intensive processing requiring extensive local storage and memory pools. Running on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs. The instance is configured with 756 GB of system RAM, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of memory per virtual core. Compute operations rely entirely on dedicated host CPUs, as the server includes zero hardware GPU accelerators.

The primary differentiator of this instance is its direct-attached storage subsystem, which provides 45,097 GB of high-performance local NVMe SSD space across 12 bundled disks. Direct host attachment minimizes I/O latency and maximizes transfer bandwidth compared to network-attached persistent storage volumes. However, because local NVMe storage is ephemeral, systems deployed on this machine require software-level data replication or automated backup mechanisms to prevent data loss in the event of host termination. From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling 45 TB of fast local storage within the instance profile reduces reliance on expensive external storage provisioned for high IOPS.

Given the density of 96 processor threads, 756 GB of memory, and comprehensive local NVMe disk arrays, the z4d-highmem-96-highlssd server type is targeted at large-scale distributed databases, NoSQL clusters, search indexing nodes, data warehousing, and high-throughput extract-transform-load (ETL) processing workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-96-highlssd is a storage-optimized instance tailored for enterprise workloads demanding massive local throughput and high compute density. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the machine provides 96 dedicated vCPUs and 756 GB of RAM, which equates to 7.88 GB of memory per virtual core. It features an integrated storage configuration containing 12 local NVMe SSDs that combine for 45,097 GB of high-speed local disk capacity, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. This architecture provides low-latency disk operations directly on the physical host, eliminating latency bottlenecks typical of network-attached storage arrays. Cost efficiency is driven by resource consolidation, combining high processing scale, expansive system memory, and direct-attached storage into a single host. The z4d-highmem-96-highlssd is engineered for high-throughput distributed databases, large-scale search indexers, data warehousing, and demanding real-time analytics pipelines.
